item.title: FDA suspends licences of 5 food outlets at Mumbai Cricket Association site
item.description: The FDA inspected 45 hotels, restaurants, eateries and dhabas during the drive, issued improvement notices to 33 establishments and conducted 25 raids ...
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food licences of five outlets at the Mumbai Cricket Association (MCA) premises over the alleged violation of food safety norms, flagging deficiencies in food handling, storage, refrigeration and sanitation.As part of its statewide drive, the FDA has suspended licences of 11 food establishments, including the five outlets at MCA, it said on Monday.The FDA inspected 45 hotels, restaurants, eateries and dhabas during the drive, issued improvement notices to 33 establishments and conducted 25 raids, according to a press note.The five MCA outlets facing action are the Permit Room, Pavilion, Mediterranean, Oriental Swing, and Clubway & Pastry Counter. The FDA inspected the outlets on August 20 and found various deficiencies related to hygiene, food handling, storage, refrigeration and sanitation.At the Permit Room, inspectors found ice accumulation in a kitchen refrigerator, an unclean and slippery floor near the kitchen entrance, inadequate temperature control, deteriorated raw material and deficiencies in food storage and handling.The outlet also lacked food-grade conformity certificates for food-contact packaging material and did not conduct regular checks of cooking oil.The Pavilion faced action after inspectors found ice accumulation and unclean refrigerator components, poor segregation of food items in cold storage, inadequate refrigeration calibration, improper thawing of frozen food and shortcomings in cooling and storage practices.At Mediterranean, the FDA found inadequate sanitisation of food equipment, improper cooling, poor portioning practices, inadequate thawing of frozen food, deficient temperature controls and shortcomings in the handling of raw materials and packaging.The Oriental Swing outlet was found to have an improperly calibrated refrigeration system, an unclean kitchen floor, damaged plaster or paint on part of the kitchen ceiling, inadequate sanitisation and deficiencies in temperature control and oil-quality checks.At the Clubway & Pastry Counter, the FDA found inadequate working space, improper storage of raw food, lack of hand gloves for a food handler and inadequate measures to prevent dust, dirt and insects from entering the food preparation area.It also found that the food business was being carried out under the name of an establishment that did not have a valid food licence. The registration certificate of the outlet was subsequently suspended, the release said.Besides the five MCA outlets, the statewide action included Lenexis Foodworks in Mahim, CafA Cadell in Shivaji Park, China Town Fast Food Centre in Mulund, Morya Misal in Warje and Saoji Upahar Gruh in Nagpur.The FDA suspended the registration of China Town Fast Food Centre with immediate effect after finding excessive use of artificial colour and MSG, repeated use of highly oxidised cooking oil, cockroach infestation, unhygienic food storage, a risk of cross-contamination between vegetarian and non-vegetarian food and inadequate drainage.The FDA also suspended the licence of Morya Misal in Pune after finding artificial colouring in food, and storage and use of expired food products.The action comes as the FDA intensifies inspections of food establishments across Maharashtra to ensure compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.

item.title: Govt appoints ex-diplomat Akbaruddin, two others to RBI central board
item.description: The central government has appointed former diplomat Syed Akbaruddin, ex-bureaucrat Annie George Mathew, and consultancy BCG India Chairman Janmejaya Kumar Sinha to RBI central board.
item.dc:creator: Press Trust of India
item.content:encoded: The central government has appointed former diplomat Syed Akbaruddin, ex-bureaucrat Annie George Mathew, and consultancy BCG India Chairman Janmejaya Kumar Sinha to RBI central board.They have been appointed as part-time, Non-official Directors on the Central Board of Reserve Bank of India for four years with effect from August 24 or until further orders, whichever is earlier, the central bank said in a release on Monday.Last week, the government had re-appointed industrialist Anand Gopal Mahindra as part-time, Non-official Director on the board.Former ISRO Chairman Somanath Sreedhara Panicker was also appointed on the board last week.Other members of the board include Revathy Iyer, a retired officer from the Indian Audit & Accounts Service, who went on to become the Deputy Comptroller and Auditor General, Government Accounts, and Sachin Chaturvedi, Director General of think tank Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS).Governor Sanjay Malhotra, deputy governors Swaminathan J, Poonam Gupta, SC Murmu and Rohit Jain, economic affairs secretary Anuradha Thakur and financial services secretary Sanjay Lohia are also on the board.

item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / India's Iran exports set to fall further amid Dubai halt, US sanctions

India's Iran exports set to fall further amid Dubai halt, US sanctions Indian exporters fear Trump's proposed "economic D-Day" plan, likely to be unveiled later on Monday, could further squeeze trade weakened by sanctions, banking caution and shipping constraints

Representative Image

Reuters NEW DELHI, Aug 24 3 min read Last Updated : Aug 24 2026 | 6:32 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Planned new U.S. sanctions on Iran and the UAE's halt on Tehran trade could severely disrupt Indian exports of rice, tea and pharmaceuticals to Iran, which have been largely routed through Dubai's port in recent years, Indian exporters said on Monday.

India has been among Iran's five largest trading partners, though bilateral trade has fallen by more than 90% from its 2018/19 highs of $17 billion, with exports now limited mostly to goods exempted on humanitarian grounds.

Indian exporters fear U.S. President Donald Trump's proposed "economic D-Day" plan, likely to be unveiled later on Monday, could further squeeze trade weakened by sanctions, banking caution and shipping constraints.

The United Arab Emirates last week suspended all trade activities, exchanges and financial transactions with Iran until further notice.

"We are already seeing indications that transactions and payment mechanisms traditionally routed through the UAE are exploring alternative jurisdictions," said Dev Garg, vice president of the Indian Rice Exporters Federation, suggesting Turkey as an alternative. Also Read

US startup Powerus builds low-cost drone interceptors amid Iran war

Vessels violating Hormuz protocols shall face fines, detention: Iran

Not a single drop of oil will be exported if US economic war persists: Iran

Entering endgame: US Treasury secy announces economic D-Day against Iran

Iran's decades-long war planning helped it withstand US-Israel strikes

EXPORTERS COULD FACE HIGHER FREIGHT AND OTHER COSTS

In the first half of 2026, India exported $383.11 million of rice to Iran - the second-largest overseas market for premium rice, including long-grained basmati.

"Any prolonged disruption in this corridor will have a much greater bearing on the basmati industry, especially on millers and exporters in northern India than on India's overall non-basmati rice trade," Garg said.

Until recently, Indian exporters typically received payment through an Indian authorised-dealer bank from a UAE trader's account - in dirhams, dollars or another permitted currency -while the trader separately collected payment from its Iranian customer through legally compliant banking channels.

Indian tea exports to Iran totalled $14.34 million in the first half of 2026. Prabhat Bezboruah, a senior tea planter and former chairman of the state-run Tea Board, said sales to Iran will be affected as a lot of that goes through the UAE.

There was no immediate comment from India's trade and foreign ministries.

A New Delhi-based exporter said direct shipments could rise, but payment problems may worsen.

Ajay Srivastava of the Global Trade Research Initiative said India's Iran trade has already fallen sharply since the previous sanctions.

"We hope food and pharmaceutical products may receive exemptions, although exporters could still face higher freight, insurance and payment costs," he said.

Iran's exports to India were dominated by crude oil, valued at about $707 million, with far smaller shipments of liquefied petroleum gas, apples, dates, almonds and kiwi fruit in the first six months of 2026. Officials have said crude oil imports from Iran were largely enabled by a U.S. exemption granted earlier this year, and may be difficult to sustain.

($1 = 95.7225 Indian rupees)
